From: Alex Rivera <alex@arborai.com>

Date: 2026-05-10T15:12:00Z
Subject: Dedicated capacity questions + workload estimation (ArborAI)

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the demo earlier — team loved the latency visibility and the cost breakdown. We're starting to sketch dedicated capacity numbers and need an opinion on the right GPU mix. High level:
- Peak QPS: ~18k short queries / min (most are <256 tokens)
- Long-context inference (background summarization & retrieval) ~2500 requests/day, avg 40k tokens, some spikes to 120k tokens
- SLOs: 95% < 120ms for short queries, long-context can be 1.5–3s
- Budget: prefer a mix that keeps unit cost predictable; open to reserved + burst.

Attached is our rough traffic workbook and a perf matrix we collected from a POC. Can you advise on H100 vs A100 vs L4 tradeoffs and a concrete starting fleet mix? Also interested in recommendations around quantization, batching, and fallback routing.

Thanks —
Alex Rivera
VP of Engineering, ArborAI

Attachments: arborai-workload-estimates.xlsx (spreadsheet), requested-perf-matrix.pdf (pdf)

Alex —

Appreciate the detail and the workbook. I skimmed the attachments and drafted an initial recommendation for us to vet internally before I share the customer-facing runbook. High-level summary up front: mixed pool — L4 for short low-latency requests, H100s for sustained long-context workloads, A100s as a cost-performance bridge and for burst/batch jobs.

I want to validate a few numbers with the ops/serving team: expected concurrency for long-context jobs, preferred latency SLO ceilings for canary, and how much burst you want to expose (e.g., on-demand vs committed burst). Hannah/Dev — can you review the recommended mixes below vs what ops would expect for headroom/tiling? Once we align I'll send this to Alex with explicit commit guidance and a suggested pilot plan.

Proposed next steps:
- Internal scoring matrix (ops + cost + reliability) — Hannah
- Pilot config (24–72h, representative prompts, KV prefix enabled) — Dev
- Canary rollout and diagnosis checklist — Irene

Thanks — sending the initial draft now.

-Sooj
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-05-10T16:10:00Z
Subject: Internal: ArborAI fleet recommendation — need numbers for proposal

Team —

Quick ask: Alex provided traffic estimates (cc'd). I sketched three candidate fleet mixes and need ops numbers to finalize the runbook. Please reply in-thread with short bullets. Candidate mixes (starter commit):

Option A — Latency-first (SLA emphasis):
- 10 x L4 (handle 80% short queries), 6 x H100 (long-context steady state), 4 x A100 (burst / batching)
- Pros: lowest tail latency for short QPS, direct routing.
- Cons: higher reserved cost for H100 headroom.

Option B — Balanced (cost + perf):
- 14 x L4, 4 x H100, 6 x A100
- Pros: lower cost per token on common path, A100 covers medium long-context and burst.
- Cons: requires careful KV caching for long jobs to prevent memory thrash.

Option C — Memory-first (long-context priority):
- 8 x L4, 10 x H100, 2 x A100
- Pros: minimizes fallback for 100k+ token sessions.
- Cons: high reserved spend; better if they commit.

Info needed from Ops:
- For each GPU type, conservative tokens/sec and tokens/dollar numbers using our inference kernels (approx).
- Expected headroom multiplier for 95th/99th tail (we usually advise 1.6–2.0x depending on burst tolerance).
- Recommended quantization levels for each model family (4-bit, 8-bit, FP16) and any impact on latency SLOs.

If you can reply by EOD I will incorporate into the customer-facing matrix and suggested commitment.

-Sooj
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-11T09:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Internal: ArborAI fleet recommendation — need numbers for proposal

Soojin / team —

Quick numbers and tradeoffs from ops + serving (high level, conservative):

Baseline hardware spec we use for sizing:
- H100 (80GB SXM): ideal for >64k token sessions and large KV caches; single card can sustain ~140–180 tokens/sec for transformer decoders at 1k context baseline when run with aggressive kernel fusion; memory headroom matters for 100k+ contexts.
- A100 (40/80GB): balanced throughput; 80GB variant handles mid-long contexts up to ~60–80k tokens with less kernel fusion efficiency than H100; single card ~220–300 tokens/sec for shorter contexts when batched (depends on batch size).
- L4 (48GB): inference-optimized for short-context, low-power latency-first workloads; excels at <2k token responses; single card ~400–700 tokens/sec for short queries when batching enabled, tail latency benefits from smaller model footprints.

Quantization & perf knobs:
- For short-query heavy paths: INT8/FP16 on L4 yields best latency/cost; minimal quality impact for most classification/generation tasks under 2k tokens.
- For long-context summarization: prefer FP16 on H100 for stability; 4-bit quantization can be considered for A100 if using quality-safeguard evals and model-specific calibration.
- KV prefix caching: will dramatically reduce H100 load for repeated retrievals; recommend enabling for anything >8k context where prefix reuse occurs.

Sizing guidance (conservative commit advice):
- Headroom: recommend 1.8x for 95/99 tail protections during initial commit; reduce after runbook-proven patterns.
- Burst policy: commit to baseline (reserve) + configured burst pool on A100s and H100s (allow controlled autoscale on L4 for short spikes).

Concrete starter recommendation for ArborAI (given their estimates and SLOs):
- Pilot commit: 10 x L4 (short queries), 5 x H100 (long-context steady), 4 x A100 (burst & medium-long).
- Rationale: H100s kept modest but sufficient to offload 24/7 long-context jobs with KV caching; L4s take the majority of short QPS and keep token cost down; A100s provide predictable batch throughput and serve as burst absorb.
- Cost mitigation: aggressive caching + per-route batching and request classification will push 60–70% of traffic to L4 path.

Operational checklist for pilot:
- 48–72h load test using ArborAI's representative prompts (they sent the workbook).
- Collect token/time histograms, tail latency, and cache hit ratio every 5m.
- Canary rule: if 95% tail >150ms for short path, throttle L4 batching and route a fraction to A100 for recovery; if long-context 95% >4s, temporarily offload to additional reserved H100 capacity or route to queued batch windows.

Irene: I'll leave canary/cutover steps to you (diagnostics and fallback playbook). Dev: please prepare pilot config and the stress script.

-Hannah
